lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: Don't touch the last door. I've been not touching it for eleven years and I'd like to keep the run going.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: My grandfather sealed it. Not a crew — him, on his own, from the inside, in the year the Quiet started. Then he took four days getting back out through the service side in the dark.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: He never said what was in there. He said there were documents behind it that people had been killed for in his century, and then he'd change the subject, and he changed the subject about it for forty years.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: You're going to open it. Everyone who comes down here is going to open it. I've met four of you. I just like to be on record as having said.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: Wheel's at the end on the left. Hasn't moved since his century, so it'll be stiff, and it'll be loud, and you'll get about one go at quiet.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: And something's been down there keeping it company all this time. It's noticed the water changing. Don't go in expecting paper.

choices.text: Not yet. He has earned eleven quiet years.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: Well. It's open. I went down after you. First time in my life I've been through that door and my grandfather spent four days on the other side of it.

lines.speaker: vault_holdout
lines.text: Nine pages. Five signatures. That's it. That's what he sealed himself in for. I've been standing here eleven years guarding nine pages and I don't understand why anybody died for it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Because it is the only copy that says who agreed to it. Everything downstream of that room has been argued about for three centuries. That is the document that ends the argument.
